validity.recommendation: Keep the row. Cite OPEC ASB 2017 Table 9.9 for Status/Length/Diameter. Note it is single-source and frozen at OPEC's 2016 snapshot; ideally seek an independent modern confirmation that the Mosul PWR ST feeder is still operating.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, and this row is a faithful transcription of a named line in an authoritative primary source. OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2017, Table 9.9 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016' (p.133-134) lists for Iraq: 'Mishraq cross road/Mousil PWR St | OPC | 38 (miles) | 12 (inches)'. I downloaded the current OPEC asset PDF (https://www.opec.org/assets/assetdb/asb-2017.pdf) and extracted the table locally (pdftotext) to confirm the exact entry, owner (OPC), length (38 mi) and diameter (12 in) — these match the GEM row exactly, i.e. GEM was populated FROM this ASB table (the odd 'Mousil'/'PWR St' spelling is verbatim from ASB). Being in the 'Main gas pipelines' table implies operating status. CAVEATS: (1) single source only — no INDEPENDENT second source names this specific line; English and Arabic searches (Iraqi press, ministry, power-station profiles) return the Mosul gas power station and the Al-Mishraq sulfur complex separately but nothing that names this feeder. Tier therefore medium, not high. (2) The data is frozen at OPEC's 2016 snapshot; the detailed gas-pipeline table was DROPPED from ASB by the 2024 edition (checked: asb-2024.pdf, 96pp, no 'PWR St' rows), so the line cannot be refreshed from newer ASBs. (3) The gem.wiki page's only outbound citation is the old opec.org static-file path for ASB 2017, which now link-rots to an HTML landing page (url_verifier returns 200 but no PDF body); the live citable copy is the asset URL above.

validity.recommendation: No reclassification needed; keep as gas. Recorded for completeness — it is a short dry-gas feeder to a power station, correctly gas transmission, not an oil/NGL line.
validity.researcher_notes: CLASSIFICATION confirmed. The line sits in OPEC ASB Table 9.9's GAS-pipeline table and its named terminus is a power station ('Mousil PWR St'), i.e. a dry-gas supply feeder to the Mosul power plant — correctly classified as gas transmission (not gathering, not process-internal). Cross-checked against the supplied GulfPub Iraq OIL/NGL roster: NONE of those crude/NGL lines is a Mishraq->Mosul line, so this is not a mis-tagged oil line. DUPLICATE check: NOT a duplicate. It is distinct from P1842 (Baiji-Al Mushraq, which is ASB's separate 'Baiji/Al-Mashriq' trunk at 131 mi/18 in per ASB, ~211 mi in GEM) — P4068 is the short 38 mi / 12 in feeder from the Mishraq crossroad to the Mosul power station. No other roster row matches its endpoints or specs.

validity.recommendation: Review three attribution fields: (a) FuelSource 'Al Mushraq' is almost certainly a mis-derivation — Al-Mishraq is a SULFUR complex, not a gas field; blank it or replace with the true dry-gas source. (b) Add operator 'Oil Pipelines Company (OPC)' per ASB (Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' is only the parent). (c) Province should be Nineveh (Ninawa), not 'Mosul' (a city); and StartLocation should be 'Mishraq cross road', not blank.
validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION caveats. (1) FuelSource='Al Mushraq' is dubious: Al-Mishraq (35.98N,43.31E, ~45 km south of Mosul) is the General Mishraq Sulphur State Company — a sulfur mine/sulfuric-acid/alum complex, NOT a gas field (Wikipedia, Britannica). 'Mishraq cross road' is the pipeline's START POINT (a road junction near that complex), so GEM appears to have back-derived a 'fuel source' from the endpoint name. The real gas source is the OPC dry-gas system (fed from the Baiji/North Gas network) tapped at that junction. (2) Operator per ASB is 'OPC' (Oil Pipelines Company / State Co. for Oil Pipelines); GEM Owner1='Iraq Ministry of Oil' is the parent ministry — accurate as owner but the operating company OPC is missing. (3) GEM StartState/Province and EndState/Province are both 'Mosul'; the correct province is Nineveh, and StartLocation is blank when ASB gives 'Mishraq cross road'.

routes.start_name: Mishraq cross road (junction near the Al-Mishraq / General Mishraq Sulphur complex, ~45 km south of Mosul)
routes.end_name: Mosul power station (Mousil PWR St), Mosul, Nineveh province
routes.corridor_desc: Short dry-gas feeder running roughly NORTH from the Mishraq crossroad (by the Al-Mishraq sulfur complex on the Tigris valley, ~45 km south of Mosul, sourced coordinate 35.9817N/43.3120E) up to a power station in/near Mosul city. GEM length is 38 mi (~61 km); straight-line Al-Mishraq->Mosul-city is ~43 km, so 61 km is consistent with a routed corridor following the Tigris valley/roads — this geometric consistency corroborates the two endpoints. Corridor is Nineveh province throughout. LOOSE bound at the north end: the exact 'Mousil PWR St' cannot be pinned to a single sourced coordinate (candidates include the Mosul gas-turbine / Al-Shemal thermal stations in the Mosul area), so the end coordinate is left null and described rather than fabricated.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the OPEC ASB line name ('Mishraq cross road' -> 'Mousil PWR St') plus geography. Start coordinate is the Al-Mishraq sulfur complex (Wikipedia: 35.981678N, 43.311989E; Britannica confirms ~45 km south of Mosul) — the crossroad is a junction adjacent to it. End is a Mosul power station (power-technology confirms a natural-gas-fired Mosul plant in Nineveh) but I could not source an exact coordinate for the specific 2016-era 'Mousil PWR St', so end_lat/lon left null (no fabricated coordinate). Length (38 mi) is geometrically consistent with a Mishraq->Mosul corridor. Suggested accuracy low: endpoints named and start pinned, but the north terminus and exact routing are unsourced.

summary: P4068 is REAL and correctly classified (gas feeder, not a duplicate): OPEC ASB 2017 Table 9.9 lists 'Mishraq cross road/Mousil PWR St, OPC, 38 mi, 12 in' verbatim — GEM was copied from it; caveats: single/stale 2016 source (medium tier) + attribution fixes (FuelSource 'Al Mushraq' is a sulfur site not a gas field, add operator OPC, province Nineveh not 'Mosul').
